cells.text: First airplane ride, in a Ford Trimotor
Joins the Boy Scouts in Upper Sandusky
Sees Purdue beat Ohio State; picks Purdue
Student pilot certificate and first solo
Earns the rank of Eagle Scout
First solo in a Navy trainer
Trains in Hawaii before the Korea cruise
Ejects after his wing hits a cable
Flies a third of his 78 Korea missions
Regular commission ends; joins the Reserve
Flies his last Korea mission, number 78
Damages the club plane in a farm field
Co-directs a campus musical at Purdue
Flies the Bell X-5 on its last program flight
First reaction-control flight in the X-1B
Flies the X-1B on its last NACA flight
Picked for Man in Space Soonest
Test subject in a centrifuge launch study
Daughter Karen diagnosed with a tumor
Flies X-15 No. 3 on its first flights

removed.reason: Month was a placeholder. Purdue's College of Engineering says he entered in September 1947 (freshman engineering). Moved to 1947-09 and confirmed.

homes.note: unchanged. Wikipedia (Hansen) says the family then moved among about 16 Ohio towns in his first 14 years (e.g. Warren, Upper Sandusky); no dated list found, so not itemised.
unchanged. Only the year 1944 is verified (Armstrong Air & Space Museum: family returned and bought 601 W. Benton St.); month is a placeholder.
unchanged; month now verified (Purdue: entered September 1947).

unchanged. Purdue says he withdrew January 1949; call-up arrived 26 Jan 1949, midshipman 24 Feb 1949, so he may only have reported in February. Also trained briefly at Corpus Christi, Texas in 1950 (no dates found).

unchanged (assigned to VF-51 on 27 Nov 1950; Wikipedia says he first served with FASRON 7 at NAS San Diego, so he may have arrived earlier in autumn 1950). Covers the Essex home port and VR-32 posting until Aug 1952.
NEW. Existing file had no Purdue return; Purdue says he returned September 1952 and graduated January 1955.
NEW. NACA Lewis lab; first test flight there 1 Mar 1955; moved to Edwards within about five months (NAE tribute). Arrival month at Cleveland not separately verified.

unchanged (reported 11 Jul 1955). Lived in Edwards bachelor quarters, wife Janet in Westwood (Los Angeles); after one semester they moved to a house in the Antelope Valley near Edwards (no date found; Juniper Hills not verified).

unchanged. NASA page: left the Flight Research Center for the Manned Spacecraft Center, Houston, September 1962. Home suburb was El Lago (Wikipedia El Lago page lists him as a resident, no dates), so 'El Lago, Texas' would be more precise.

CHANGED from 'Cincinnati, Ohio'. He taught at the University of Cincinnati (NASA page: resigned from NASA Aug 1971, professor 1971-1979) but lived on a 300-acre farm near Lebanon, Ohio (NAE tribute; Wikipedia 'Lebanon, Ohio' says he made his home there 23 years). Start month taken from the NASA resignation; farm purchase date not verified.

NEW, approximate. He divorced Janet in 1994, married Carol Knight 12 Jun 1994 and they lived in Indian Hill (Cincinnati suburb); move date not found, month is the wedding month. Died 25 Aug 2012 at Mercy Health Fairfield Hospital, Fairfield, Ohio.

notes: COVERAGE IS BELOW TARGET (about 12% of months filled, 10.6% confirmed). The shared WebSearch budget ran out part way through, so everything after that came from direct page fetches only. No 'news' cells: no newspaper archive (NYT, Ohio/Indiana papers, Chronicling America, Purdue Exponent, Wapakoneta Daily News) could be searched. Google Books (Hansen, First Man) was blocked by a captcha and I did not try to get round it; Britannica, Ohio History Connection, nationalaviation.org and Purdue archives returned 403, and history.navy.mil failed TLS, so the NHHC dates (first carrier landing 2 Mar 1950; commission ended 25 Feb 1952; Reserve resignation 21 Oct 1960) are cited from search-result snippets and cross-checked against Wikipedia (which cites Hansen 2005). Most Navy/NACA day-level dates rest on the English Wikipedia article (Hansen pp. 68-134); I opened and read its wikitext, not Hansen. Weakest areas: 1930-1945 childhood (only the Warren flight, July 1936, a date from a Warren volunteer group that Hansen hedges), 1947-48, 1953-54 at Purdue, 1956-1959 at Edwards, 1961 (only Karen's diagnosis and the Dec X-15-3 flights). Unverified, from memory only, so NOT included: births of Eric (about mid-1957), Karen (about 1959) and Mark (1963); sibling births (June, Dean); Eagle Scout and Blume graduation months; summer 1961 Dyna-Soar trips to Seattle (NAE tribute, no month); James Michener visit to Essex 'late 1951'; Air Medal/Gold Star award months (Purdue archive snippets conflict: citation for operations from 11 Dec 1951, another dated 1 Dec 1952); Paresev flights (undated); X-15 'ball nose' first flight (undated). Placeholder-month cells (confirmed false): 1941-09 Scout troop (year 1941 only), 1944-01 Wapakoneta (1944 only), 1947-03 Eagle Scout (1947 only), 1947-05 Blume graduation (1947 only), 1954-05 Aeronca incident (1954 only), 1959-06 Johnsville centrifuge (Encyclopedia Astronautica dates the program 18 Jun 1959, unclear if that is his run), 1960-04 Dyna-Soar (Wikipedia X-20 page says seven pilots secretly chosen April 1960, citing van Pelt; the Armstrong article says he joined the pilot consultant group Nov 1960 (Hansen pp. 171-173); NAE says 'secretly named in 1960'). 1945-10 is deduced: Armstrong's article says he saw Purdue beat Ohio State at Ohio Stadium in 1945; the 1945 Ohio State season article gives that game as 20 Oct 1945 (Purdue 35-13). 1957-11, 1958-01 (X-1B flights 25 and 27, 27 Nov 1957 and 23 Jan 1958) come from Encyclopedia Astronautica's X-1B flight log, consistent with NASA's 'Bell X-1B (4 flights, first on August 15, 1957)'. 1955-10 X-5: NASA page says his one X-5 flight, the last in the program, was 25 Oct 1955. X-15 dates (30 Nov 1960, 9 Dec 1960, 19/20 Dec 1961) are from Wikipedia's List of X-15 flights (Jenkins/McDowell); NASA's page confirms 30 Nov 1960. Discrepancy: NHHC snippet gives 23 Aug 1950 for qualification, Wikipedia says notified 16 Aug, ceremony 23 Aug; same month. Locations: no residence evidence found for Juniper Hills; Armstrong's Houston-area home was El Lago; Washington, D.C. (Deputy Associate Administrator for Aeronautics, 1969/70-1971, sources conflict on start) could be a stay but residence there is not verified; no later overseas tour or Gemini/Apollo trip lasts months, so no stays after 1952 are proposed.
